Summary: Enterprise POC for Redwood Dedicated to replace a mixed self-host + cloud setup for customer-facing chat and reranking. They run global maritime ops dashboards, strict residency for EU manifests, and sub-100ms median goal for short chat flows. Customer requested guaranteed throughput for peak ordering windows (sustained 600 qps across 8 concurrent routes) and a 95th-percentile latency SLO target for token generation.

Primary objectives: validate dedicated GPU planning (N GPUs per shard), confirm continuous batching doesn't violate 100ms SLO for single-turn chat, exercise prefix/KV caching for repeated manifest lookups, and run soak tests for 48 hours at 70% and 100% of target load.

What we've done so far: kick-off call (see ff_2026-02-28), baseline run on hosted models to establish production tokens/sec, initial dedicated cluster spun up (4 x A100-equivalent), and synthetic load tests executed against 4 representative prompt families. SE (Diego) provided quantization recommendations and suggested model routing: large-chat -> quantized 16-bit variant for bursty traffic, fallback to smaller 7B variant for extreme scaling.

Customer comments: 'We need certainty on throughput during seasonal peaks — SLA credits need to be clear and enforceable.' CT O follow-up: wants explicit network egress amortization in pricing.

POC plan attachments in Drive include representative-prompts.csv and a soak-test checklist. Next workshop planned 2026-03-12 to review soak-test telemetry and tune autoscaler policies.

Sales shorthand / quick bullets:
- POC goal: validate reserved GPU count for 600 sustained qps and <120ms 95p token latency on chat flows.
- Acceptance: soak test at 72h with no SLO breaches and realistic routing fallbacks triggered during induced node failure.
- Pricing ask: committed monthly minimum with upward burst capacity.
- Risk: legal wants explicit recovery SLA if model variant fallback increases average token cost.
